chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Abu Suleiman al-Hammar, who said:

We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he brought us a sauce (madiarah) and food after it. Then he brought a basket of soft dates (rutab) upon which were various kinds. So he (peace be upon him) took one with his hand after another, saying: 'What do you call this?' So we said such and such, until he took one and said: 'What do you call this?' So we said: 'Al-Mushan'. He said: 'We call it Umm Jirzan. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was brought something from it, so he ate from it and supplicated for it, so there is nothing from the palm trees that bears more than it.'

key_terms.أُمَّ جِرْذَانَ: A specific name for a variety of dates, literally 'Mother of the Rat'.
key_terms.الْمُشَانَ: A specific name for a variety of dates.
key_terms.رُطَبٍ: Soft, ripe dates, still on the palm or recently harvested.
key_terms.قِنَاعٍ: A basket or container, often woven.
key_terms.مَضِيرَةٍ: A type of sauce or dip, often made from dates or other ingredients.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the date variety 'Umm Jirzan' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s pedagogical method of engaging companions in naming specific date varieties, culminating in the identification of 'Umm Jirzan' (also known as 'Al-Mushan'). It establishes the Prophet’s practice of consuming and supplicating for this variety, affirming its status as the most prolific palm fruit, a detail that underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Sunnah in daily sustenance and appreciating the natural blessings (*ni'mat*) mentioned in the Quran.
